title: three-sided fence area and domain
stem: A rectangular pen borders a straight river, so no fence is needed along the river. Exactly 40 meters of fence covers the other three sides. If x is the width perpendicular to the river, which single-variable area function and physical domain should be optimized?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: Only one perpendicular side is subtracted; the enclosure requires two fenced widths.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: Correct: Two widths use 2x of the 40 units of fence, leaving river-parallel length 40−2x. Area is width times that length, and both must be positive.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: This subtracts four widths as if all sides used equal fence, contrary to the three-sided constraint.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: The factor 2 counts two copies of the area rather than the single rectangle's area.

title: open-top box volume and domain
stem: An open-top box is made by cutting an x-by-x square from every corner of a square sheet with side 12 inches, then folding up the flaps. Which volume function and allowable positive x interval give the optimization problem?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: A base side loses two cut lengths, not one; this overstates the base and domain.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: Correct: Each base side loses x at each end, becoming 12−2x; the folded height is x. A positive base requires x<6.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: This omits one base dimension and has area units rather than volume units.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: This gives base area but omits the height x needed for volume.

title: open-top box volume and domain (variant 2)
stem: An open-top box is made by cutting x-by-x squares from the four corners of a 24-inch square sheet and folding up the flaps. Among boxes with positive height and base dimensions, which cut size produces the greatest volume, and what is that volume?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cut x=12 inches; the maximum volume is 0 cubic inches.
choices.rationale: A cut of 12 leaves zero base dimensions and is outside the positive-volume domain.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cut x=4 inches; the maximum volume is 1,024 cubic inches.
choices.rationale: Correct: The domain is 0<x<12, and V=x(24−2x)². Its derivative is (24−2x)(24−6x), so the interior critical point is x=4; V(4)=4(16)²=1,024, while volume tends to zero at both domain boundaries.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cut x=6 inches; the maximum volume is 864 cubic inches.
choices.rationale: The stated volume at x=6 is correct, but V'(6)<0 and it is smaller than V(4).

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cut x=8 inches; the maximum volume is 512 cubic inches.
choices.rationale: The stated volume at x=8 is correct, but it is smaller than V(4).

title: cost-weighted cylinder objective
stem: A cylindrical container must hold 100π cubic units. It has two circular caps. Material for each circular face costs 1 currency units per square unit, and material for the curved side costs 1 per square unit. If r>0 is the radius and h is height, which cost function of r alone should be minimized?

choices.label: A
choices.rationale: The curved area is 2πrh; dropping its factor 2 undercounts side material.

choices.label: B
choices.rationale: Substituting h=V/(πr²) makes the curved cost proportional to 1/r, not r.

choices.label: C
choices.rationale: Correct: The volume constraint πr²h=100π gives h=100/r². Face cost is 2πr²; curved-side cost is 1(2πrh)=200π/r. Any r>0 gives a positive h.

choices.label: D
choices.rationale: Radius has no lower bound of the numerical volume; every positive radius yields a positive height.
